response: Tens of thousands marched through central London on Saturday under the Together Alliance, with trade unions, anti-racism campaigners, and Muslim representative bodies uniting to protest what they label the far-right. This follows just six months after one of Britain's largest-ever far-right demonstrations and comes weeks before key local elections. In truth, this has nothing to do with defending anyone from hate. It is a coalition of left-wing activists and identity groups flexing their muscle to shut down debate on immigration, national identity, and the preservation of traditional British culture. They are framing ordinary concerns over social order and cultural continuity as bigotry, all in an attempt to influence the coming elections and push further progressive changes that erode personal responsibility and family structures in favor of division and institutional overhaul.
